stem: Humidity is consistently higher inside a dense canopy than at the room wall sensor. What is the strongest lesson?
choices: Room averages can miss crop-zone microclimates, so canopy-relevant measurements matter
Wall sensors should always be removed
Humidity differences prove disease is present
Canopy density has no relationship to local airflow
rationale: Crop-zone conditions can differ from wall or room-average conditions, particularly in dense canopies with restricted air exchange.
